skill.name: wrangler
skill.description: Use the Cloudflare Wrangler CLI to inspect, deploy, and manage Workers, Pages, KV, R2, D1, secrets, and account authentication.
skill.summary: Focused Wrangler command reference for Cloudflare deployment and operations tasks.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced bash examples in SKILL.md. No prompt injection attempt or hidden executable source code was found. The skill is a legitimate Wrangler command reference, but several examples can modify Cloudflare resources or handle secrets and should require user confirmation.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running deploys, KV or R2 writes, D1 migrations, Pages deploys, or secret updates.
Avoid placing real secret values in prompts, logs, or command transcripts. Prefer secure Wrangler prompts or environment-specific secret workflows.
Verify the Cloudflare account, environment, namespace, bucket, database, or project before running any command that reads or changes resources.

content.value_statement: Cloudflare teams need quick, consistent commands for Workers, Pages, storage, databases, and secrets. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused Wrangler reference for common deployment and operations tasks.
actual_capabilities: Lists deployed Workers, Pages projects, KV namespaces, R2 buckets, and D1 databases.
Provides Wrangler commands to deploy Workers and Pages projects.
Shows how to tail Worker logs and run a Worker locally.
Gives examples for reading and writing KV keys and uploading R2 objects.
Includes D1 query and migration commands for database operations.
Covers secret setup, secret listing, authentication checks, and login.
limitations: Does not install Wrangler or configure Cloudflare accounts.
Requires valid Cloudflare authentication and project configuration before commands work.
Does not validate command targets, permissions, or production safety.
Uses generic placeholders that must be replaced with real project values.

prompt_templates.title: Check Wrangler Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wrangler skill to check my current Cloudflare authentication and list available Workers without changing resources.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Worker
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wrangler skill to prepare the steps to deploy my current Worker project. Ask me before running any deploy command.

prompt_templates.title: Review Storage State
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wrangler skill to list KV namespaces, R2 buckets, and D1 databases for this account. Summarize findings and do not read object contents unless I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wrangler skill to create an execution plan for Workers, Pages, D1 migrations, and secrets. Include confirmations before every command that changes production.

output: Confirms the active Cloudflare account before deployment.

output_examples.input: Show me what Cloudflare storage exists for this account.
output: Lists KV namespaces, R2 buckets, and D1 databases separately.
Summarizes resource names and likely next actions.
Avoids reading stored values unless the user approves.
Identifies the target database and migration intent.
Recommends a confirmation step before applying changes.
Notes rollback and verification checks for the release.

best_practices: Confirm the Cloudflare account and environment before mutating resources.
Run read-only list commands before deploys, writes, or migrations.
Keep secret values out of prompts, chat history, and command logs.
anti_patterns: Running deploy or migration commands without explicit user approval.
Replacing placeholders with production identifiers before confirming the environment.
Pasting real secret values into prompts or command transcripts.

faq.question: What does this skill help manage?
faq.answer: It helps with common Wrangler commands for Cloudflare Workers, Pages, KV, R2, D1, secrets, and login checks.

faq.question: Does it install Wrangler?
faq.answer: No. Wrangler must already be installed and available in the environment where commands run.

faq.question: Does it require Cloudflare authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. Most commands require an authenticated Cloudflare account with the correct permissions.

faq.question: Can it change production resources?
faq.answer: Yes. Deploy, write, migration, and secret commands can affect production resources if pointed there.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use secure Wrangler flows and avoid placing real secret values in chat, logs, or shared transcripts.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives each tool a concise reference for Wrangler-based Cloudflare operations.
